instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbying as a lobbyist is prohibited unless the person is licensed and authorized (§13.66), and individuals paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying are defined as “lobbyist” (§13.62(11)), subject only to limited exemptions such as the ≤$500 verified-statement option (§13.621(5)).
A lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, requiring renewal on a biennial (24-month) cycle.
Lobbyists must obtain their own license (§13.63), while principals must separately file a registration statement with specified information (§13.64(1)).
The lobbyist license application must include items such as a social security number and signature, but there is no statutory requirement to submit a photograph.

An agency that files under §13.695 and named officials are not subject to several lobbying provisions (§13.621(2)), and specified public officials/employees are not subject to key requirements when acting in an official capacity (§13.621(3)).

State agencies that file a §13.695 statement (and named officials) are exempt from multiple sections (e.g., licensing/registration/reporting) except as provided in §13.695, providing partial relief compared to nongovernment actors.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections specify a 10-day change-notice rule only for agencies filing under §13.695(2), not for lobbyists’ license or principals’ registration changes; no lobbyist change-notification deadline is provided in the included text.

The included text requires licensure/authorization before lobbying (§13.66) but does not state a numeric ‘days after first lobbying’ registration deadline for lobbyists; thus the days value cannot be derived.
